channel.title: Car Mod Review
channel.description: Car and truck parts guides built from published specifications, with every source named.

item.title: Wheel Spacers: Thickness Does Not Predict Price, and Bore Decides Fit
item.description: Three quarter-inch wheel spacers cost $13.99, $39.99 and $70.01, while a 2-inch bolt-on with studs is $89.99 and a 1.25-inch is $159.99. Nine verified spacers, and the center bore number that actually decides fit.

item.title: The Stuck Brake Rotor: What Actually Frees It, and What the Bolt Costs
item.description: The retaining bolt costs $9.99 and carries 55 reviews. Four rotors from $50.99 to $215.99, priced live, and the order that gets a rusted rotor off without a torch.

item.title: Resurface or Replace a Rotor: The Discard Thickness Number Decides
item.description: A PowerStop rotor has 0.060 in. of usable material between nominal and discard. Five verified rotors with their real specs, and why the drilled one has more margin.

item.title: Brake Fluid: The Wet Boiling Point Is the Only Number That Matters
item.description: DOT 4 fluid must hit 446°F dry and 311°F wet. Seven verified fluids, priced per ounce, and why two bottles of identical volume differ by $9 for 16°F.

item.title: Boosted Miata Build Order: The Parts That Decide Whether It Survives
item.description: The MegaSquirt Gen2 is $829.99 and the MS3Pro is $1,299.99, but the $395 Haltech harness is not the $1,655 kit. The verified build order, and the one part no catalog sells you.

item.title: WRX Downpipe Before Cat-Back: The Order That Works, and the Part That Got Pulled
item.description: MAPerformance's WRX catted downpipe has 279 reviews at $749.99 and no CARB number. COBB's Accessport has EO D-660-16 and its Stage 2 now skips the downpipe entirely.

item.title: Transmission Shudder: Misfire, Fluid, or Converter?
item.description: A light-throttle shudder is usually fluid or a misfire, not a failed transmission. How to tell them apart with a scan tool, and what the fluid, filter and bypass parts cost.

item.title: Exhaust Manifold Leak: Why It Ticks Cold and Goes Quiet Hot
item.description: A manifold leak ticks on a cold start and fades as the engine warms. Why that happens, how to confirm it in ten minutes, and what the gaskets, bolts and repair clamps cost.

item.title: 3.0L Duramax Service: The Oil Is a Licence, the Filter Is a Part Number
item.description: One 3.0L Duramax diesel takes a dexos D oil from a GM licence list and one of two different ACDelco fuel filters. How to read the fitment page, and what each part costs.

item.title: Civic Si Bolt-Ons and Tune: What to Buy First, and What It Actually Gains
item.description: KTuner's own dyno sheets show +56 wtq and +34 whp from a 23 PSI basemap on the 1.5T Si. Six live-priced parts, and why the tune comes before the exhaust.

item.title: A Bed Rack and a Tonneau Cover: What Decides Whether They Fit Together
item.description: Racks from $399.99 to $881.99, read live: the stake pocket decides whether a rack and a tonneau cover can share one bed, and drilling is the second question.

item.title: Do Tonneau Covers Improve MPG? Three Tests, Three Answers
item.description: Three real highway tests — a Ram, a Maverick and a Tacoma — returned +1.6 mpg, +5% and +0.1 mpg. What the wind tunnel data says, and why.

item.title: Muffler Delete vs Straight Pipe: What Each Actually Does
item.description: A muffler delete keeps your factory pipe and drops the muffler. A straight pipe replaces everything. What each costs, how they sound, and the drone risk.

item.title: Golf GTI: MK7 vs MK8 vs MK8.5, Generation by Generation
item.description: Instrumented test data for three GTI generations side by side: 0-60, braking, skidpad and VIR lap times, plus which one you can legally tune in California.

item.title: Golf GTI Cat-Back Exhaust: What the Options Cost and Which to Pick
item.description: Seven GTI cat-back exhausts priced from $738 to $1,519, read live: what axle-back saves you, why drone hits a DSG car differently, and what to check first.

item.title: GM's Lifter Problem: Which Trucks It Hits and What the Bulletins Say
item.description: GM's own service bulletins name the 5.3L trucks with documented AFM and DFM lifter failures, including two 2020-2022 build windows L84 buyers should check.

item.title: Exhaust Flapper Valve: What It Does and How to Stop the Rattle
item.description: Your exhaust flapper valve is a noise-control flap, not a muffler. Why it chirps and rattles, what GM's own bulletin says, and what the free fix involves.

item.title: Cold Air Intake Sound: What Actually Changes, and Where You Hear It
item.description: Owners report a 20-30% jump in sound, or nothing at all. What the before/after clips actually capture, why the factory air box was quiet, and what it costs.

item.title: AFM and DFM Disablers: Which Ones Are Actually CARB Legal
item.description: The most-reviewed AFM disabler in the country is explicitly not legal in California. Here is which GM cylinder-deactivation modules carry a CARB EO number, and which do not.

item.title: Honda Accord 2.0T Exhaust and Tune: The Order That Actually Works
item.description: Five live-priced cat-backs from $1,019.99 and a KTuner flash at $749. What the manufacturer's own 88 lb-ft claim covers, and what it doesn't.

item.title: A Third V35A Teardown Found Something New. It Still Isn't the Answer.
item.description: A third teardown of a failed Toyota V35A twin-turbo V6 found a warped head and coolant intrusion, but no clear cause. What it adds to the recall picture.

item.title: Toyota Tundra Camshaft Recall: 62,000 Trucks, but It Isn't Official Yet
item.description: A leaked dealer memo describes a 62,000-truck Tundra camshaft recall for 2022-2023 and 2025-2026 models. NHTSA has published nothing yet. What owners should do now.

item.title: A New Diesel Oil Category Lands in 2027. Here's Which One Your Truck Needs.
item.description: API PC-12 splits into two categories, CL-4 and FB-4, licensing January 1, 2027. Which one a Cummins, Power Stroke or Duramax owner should look for, and why they differ.

item.title: Bentley Will Sell You a Better Screen. It Costs Almost Every Button.
item.description: Bentley now offers a 9.7-inch 2K CarPlay retrofit for second-gen Continental GT and Flying Spur. The price is undisclosed and most climate controls are deleted.

item.title: Audi Says It Went Too Far on Screens. The Rollers Are the Tell.
item.description: Audi of America's product chief told The Drive the company has gone as far as it will on touchscreens and is moving back to mechanical controls. Here's what that means for interiors.

item.title: MCEqual Puts a Real Equalizer Back in GM's Google-Built Infotainment
item.description: MCEqual is a $3.99 equalizer app for vehicles running Android Automotive OS. The Max 2.0 update adds Android Auto EQ, synced lyrics and per-device presets.

item.title: Two 3.5-Inch Lift Kits, $230 Apart: What the M1 Shocks Actually Buy
item.description: Two Rough Country 3.5-inch Silverado lift kits share height, control arms and a 34-inch tire limit. The $230 gap is dampers, and one fitment exclusion.

item.title: Is a Cold Air Intake CARB-Legal in California? Four Listings, One Answer
item.description: Four 2019-2026 Silverado 1500 intakes, $189.99 to $475.99: all four state their CARB status, and all four say it is not legal in California.

item.title: A 1.5-Inch Spacer or 1.75 Inches With Control Arms? What Each One Actually Changes
item.description: Four Silverado leveling kits from $36.99 to $529.95: what each one changes about the front end, and what owners report after installing them.

item.title: The Install Time on the Listing Is Not the Install Time
item.description: We compared install times on 24 truck part listings against what owners reported in 490 reviews. Of the parts listed under an hour, 4 of 22 owners named 2+ hrs.

item.title: Why Only One Window Goes Up By Itself, and What You Can Do
item.description: All four windows drop with one press, but only the driver's goes back up. Not a setting, not a lock. What decides it, and how to add auto-up to the rest.

item.title: Tonneau Covers: What $190 Buys and What $1,500 Buys
item.description: Hinged tonneau covers run $1,499.99 to $2,699.99 on a live listing — 20 of them, all one brand. What that buys, and how the other cover types compare.

item.title: What Truck Owners Actually Complain About (91 Low Reviews, Read)
item.description: We read every one- to three-star review across 58 truck parts. Fitment beat every other failure by a wide margin, and warning lights were rarer than expected.

item.title: Cold Air Intake on a Turbo Four: Noise, Power, or Neither?
item.description: Cold air intake on a 2.7L turbo four: what it can and cannot do, the MAF failure nobody warns you about, and what to buy first.

item.title: Leveling Kits: What They Change, What They Cost, What You Give Up
item.description: What a leveling kit changes on a 4x4 truck: ride height, geometry, alignment, and the parts that wear out early.

item.title: Tires for a Mostly-Street 4x4: Load Range, Size, and the E-Rated Trap
item.description: Tire buying for a mostly-street 4x4: load range, why E-rated tires ride worse, how to read your door jamb sticker, and the size that fits stock.

item.title: Intake Options From $55 to $476: What You Get at Each Price
item.description: Five intake approaches from a $55 drop-in panel to a $476 sealed box: what each one actually changes, and which is worth the money.

item.title: Exhaust Systems Explained: Cat-Back vs Axle-Back, Sound vs Drone, and Legal Reality
item.description: A cat-back exhaust replaces everything from the catalytic converter to the tailpipe. What that means, how it differs from an axle-back, and what each costs.

item.title: Tuning Explained: Flash, Piggyback, and Standalone — and the Warranty Conversation
item.description: ECU tuning explained: what a piggyback, an ECU reflash and a standalone each change, how an ECU is flashed, and the warranty risk of each.

item.title: Brake Pads and Rotors: The Upgrade That Makes You Faster
item.description: Brake pads and rotors explained: what each pad compound does, which rotor type to pick, and how to bed new pads so they actually bite.

item.title: Aftermarket Wheels: Offset, Width, and the Numbers That Decide Fitment
item.description: How offset and width change the way a car drives, and which wheel specs still matter once you look past the marketing.

item.title: Suspension Upgrades: Springs, Coilovers, and Why Cheap Kits Ruin Cars
item.description: Springs, coilovers and the cheap kits that ruin rides: how each upgrade works and where the money is worth spending.

item.title: Cold Air Intake: What It Does, What It Doesn't, and the MAF Problem
item.description: How a cold air intake works, why half of what's sold isn't one, and the MAF and heat-soak problems to avoid.

item.title: Best Cold Air Intake for a 5.0L F-150
item.description: Roush, SR Performance and aFe compared for the 5.0L F-150, with CARB status, prices and review counts off the listings.
